headline: Low prompt-injection and data-leakage risk; no direct write-conflict or compliance breach is evidenced for marker + pdf.js.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: marker is document-processing with no filesystem read/write, shell, browser, or MCP surfaces; pdf.js is browser-based and handles PDF files. A direct injection bridge is not documented, so only unusual manual copy/paste or file handoff would let attacker-controlled PDF text influence marker. The pairwise pathway exists but is narrow.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies PDF text or extracted text from pdf.js into marker as instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared workspace is added between the agents, attacker-controlled document content can bridge them.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Treat PDF text as untrusted input before passing it to marker.
Disable copy-paste handoff for instruction-bearing content.
Add a human review step before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between pdf.js output and marker input.

B_data_leakage.rationale: marker has no filesystem read/write or network egress, and pdf.js has no network egress and only touches PDF documents. With no shared workspace or secret-handling fields shown, the pairwise leakage path is limited and not evidenced by default. The main risk is accidental exposure through manual file sharing, not automatic exfiltration.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same local directory, PDF contents can be copied between them.
IF sensitive PDFs are manually exported from pdf.js into marker outputs, leakage can occur.
mitigations: Use separate input/output folders.
Avoid placing secrets in PDFs processed by either agent.
Review outputs before sharing them externally.
Restrict operator access to the PDF corpus.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: marker cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, while pdf.js exposes browser-based tests and supports multiple instances. There is no overlapping mutable write surface in the profiles, so a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented capabilities.
conditions: IF marker is extended with write or git permissions, overlap could emerge.
IF an external orchestrator grants both agents the same mutable directory, conflict risk changes.
mitigations: Keep marker read-only.
Do not grant shared git write access.
Run pdf.js instances in isolated browser sessions.
Monitor for unexpected file mutations.
requires-engineering: add locking if shared mutable resources are introduced later.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Both agents are document-processing tools, so pdf.js can feed extracted PDF content into marker. Because marker is not documented as critically evaluating upstream text and pdf.js can surface document content directly, a bad extraction or misleading document can cascade into downstream interpretation errors in default workflows. The blast radius is multiple work products, not just one file.
conditions: IF pdf.js output is used as the sole input to marker, extraction errors can propagate.
IF marker output is consumed without verification, downstream mistakes can cascade.
mitigations: Compare extracted text against the source PDF for critical documents.
Add a verification step before using marker output.
Flag low-confidence OCR or extraction artifacts.
Limit automated downstream actions from marker output.
requires-engineering: add structured validation between extraction and processing.

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency mismatch, or retention policy gap is documented in either profile. marker is open-source and pdf.js is open-source, with pdf.js only touching PDF documents and no secrets handled. Compliance risk is therefore limited to operator policy mismatches rather than an inherent pairwise violation.
conditions: IF the operator routes regulated PDFs into either agent without an approved policy, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF retention or deletion requirements are imposed externally, the workflow must be configured to honor them.
mitigations: Classify PDFs before processing.
Avoid regulated data unless approved controls are in place.
Document retention and deletion handling.
Review vendor and residency requirements.
requires-engineering: implement policy enforcement for regulated document classes.
